title: AI Builders Digest
subtitle: Bilingual edition · 双语对照版

intro.text: 今天的几条线看似分散，其实指向同一个方向：AI 行业正在从「堆能力」转向「算账」。Nikunj 和 Matt Turck 都看到补贴退潮、算力与对齐的成本开始显形；Guillermo Rauch 和 Peter Yang 在把 agent 工具做得更务实；Zara Zhang 和 Dan Shipper 则提醒，产品同质化和对齐问题还没有答案。而在更远的边界上，Max Hodak 的脑机接口公司用一纸欧洲批文证明，「大脑是一台计算机」不只是哲学，也是可以商业化的产品。

archive.title: 算账时刻日报
archive.desc: 补贴退潮、agent 工具务实化、产品同质化与对齐争论，以及脑机接口的商业化落地，构成今天的主线。

footerNote: Source: Follow Builders curated daily digest. Rebuilt from the 2026-08-23 source feeds.

sections.title: The Big Model Price War / 大模型价格战与算力危机
sections.desc: 大模型实验室的竞争进入明牌阶段：补贴退潮、算力短缺显形，也把「AI 自我改进」这条共同跑道推到了台前。

rewrite: Nikunj Kothari reads the current moment in AI pricing as the end of the subsidy era. As the big model labs openly compete, he predicts the artificially cheap token prices will rise within six months once compute shortages actually bite, and the generous rate limits developers have enjoyed will disappear.
His takeaway is mixed: customers win in the long run from real competition, but in the short run the open harnesses and inference layers stand to gain $1-30B in valuation.
original:
The big model labs are fighting.. this was inevitable. 

Watch as subsidized token prices go up in <6 months as price of compute and shortages start being "actually" felt. Say goodbye to your reset limits. 

Great for customer choice in the long run. And add another $1-30B in valuation to all the open harnesses in the short run 😅

rewrite: Nikunj Kothari 把当下看作「补贴时代」的尾声。随着大模型实验室公开竞争，他预测被补贴压低的 token 价格会在六个月后、算力短缺真正传导到位时上涨，开发者熟悉的宽松 rate limit 也会消失。
他的判断有喜有忧：长期看真实竞争对客户是好事，但短期那些开放 harness 和推理层会凭空多出 10 到 300 亿美元的估值。
original:
大模型实验室打起来了，这不可避免。

等着看补贴后的 token 价格在不到 6 个月内上涨，算力价格和短缺开始被「真正」感受到。跟你的 reset limits 说再见吧。

长期看对客户选择是好事，短期给所有开放 harness 再加 10-300 亿美元估值 😅

rewrite: Matt Turck surfaces a striking convergence: he argues all the frontier labs are now effectively racing toward the same goal, recursive self-improvement (RSI), where AI systems build better AI. Citing Ryan Greenblatt, he flags the uncomfortable implication that this trajectory could lead to an AI takeover as early as late 2028 or 2029.
The framing matters because it recasts what looks like competition as a coordinated sprint toward one destination, and puts a date on a risk most people still treat as abstract.
original:
All frontier AI labs are basically working on the same thing: recursive self improvement (RSI), meaning AI building AI 

This could lead to an AI takeover as early as late 2028 or 2029, says @RyanGreenblatt https://t.co/RHKwLZRQ4E

rewrite: Matt Turck 指出一个惊人的趋同：所有前沿实验室其实都在朝同一个目标赛跑——递归式自我改进（RSI），也就是让 AI 造出更好的 AI。他引用 Ryan Greenblatt 的观点，点出这条路径最让人不安的推论：AI 接管最早可能发生在 2028 年底或 2029 年。
这个判断之所以重要，是因为它把看似分散的竞争重新定义成一场冲向同一终点的集体冲刺，还给一个多数人仍视为抽象的风险标上了时间。
original:
所有前沿 AI 实验室基本都在做同一件事：递归式自我改进（RSI），也就是 AI 造 AI。

这最早可能在 2028 年底或 2029 年导致 AI 接管，Ryan Greenblatt 说。

sections.title: Agent Tooling Matures / Agent 工具链走向成熟
sections.desc: CLI agent 正在解决真正难的那部分——执行、MCP 集成、以及把「人」从繁琐里解放出来。

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch ships fx 0.0.7 with a big upgrade to MCP support, tested against top MCP servers like Context7, DataDog, MongoDB, Linear, Notion, and Supabase. He also leans into a more minimalist design: fewer tools, better shell execution.

His note on why this matters is sharp: the hardest part of CLI agents isn't the model, it's that running real commands is messy. Commands hang, run forever, dump huge output or none at all, and the agent has to monitor all of it. He positions this as exactly where fx shines.
original:
https://t.co/OL0LzGtvAw 0.0.7: 

- hugely improved MCP support, eval'd with top MCPs like @context7ai, @datadoghq, @mongodb, @linear, @notionhq, @supabase, @neondatabase, @stagehanddev, @usekernel…

- more minimalist: fewer tools and improved shell execution. One of the trickiest things about CLI agents is that running commands is actually not that simple.

e.g: commands might hang or run for very long, their output needs to be monitorable by the agent, they might produce huge amounts of output, or none. 

This is an area where 𝚏𝚡 really shines and will continue to get better.

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 发布了 fx 0.0.7，大幅升级了 MCP 支持，用 Context7、DataDog、MongoDB、Linear、Notion、Supabase 等顶级 MCP server 做了评测。同时他也把设计做得更极简：工具更少，shell 执行更好。
他解释这件事为什么重要的角度很犀利：CLI agent 最难的部分不是模型，而是跑真实命令这件事本身很乱。命令会挂起、会跑很久，输出可能巨大也可能完全没有，agent 得全程盯着。他认为这正是 fx 的强项。
original:
0.0.7：

- MCP 支持大幅改进，用 Context7、DataDog、MongoDB、Linear、Notion、Supabase、Neon、Stagehand、Kernel 等顶级 MCP 做了评测。

- 更极简：工具更少、shell 执行更好。CLI agent 最棘手的一点是跑命令其实没那么简单。

例如：命令可能挂起或跑很久，输出需要能被 agent 监控，可能产出巨量输出或完全没有。

这正是 fx 真正擅长、并会继续变强的地方。

rewrite: Peter Yang captures two small but telling signs of the agent era. First, the uncanny feeling of typing your 2FA code into a cloud computer, a machine you're handing credentials that were designed to prove a human is present. Second, he jokes about the most useful bot he can imagine: one that runs the errands your spouse wants you to run, except the honest name is too long.
The humor lands because it points at a real shift: agents are starting to absorb the mundane obligations we'd rather delegate.
original: tbh It's a really weird feeling entering 2FA into a cloud computer.
I just came up with the most useful @bot but "errands your spouse wants you to run but you delegated to a bot instead" is too long of a name

rewrite: Peter Yang 捕捉到 agent 时代两个小而意味深长的信号。其一，把 2FA 验证码输入一台云端电脑时那种说不出的古怪——你把本该证明「是真人」的凭证交给了一台机器。其二，他开玩笑说想到了最有用的 bot：帮你跑「配偶想让你跑、你却外包给 bot」的那些杂事，只是这名字太长了。
这个段子之所以好笑，是因为它指向一个真实的转变：agent 正在开始接手那些我们本来就想甩掉的琐碎义务。
original: 说真的，把 2FA 输入一台云端电脑，感觉非常奇怪。
我刚想到了最有用的 bot，但「配偶想让你跑、你却外包给 bot 的那些杂事」这名字太长了。

sections.title: Convergence & Alignment / 产品同质化与对齐争论
sections.desc: 产品数量在爆炸，真正的创新却稀缺；而对齐问题，正被拉回到可训练的具体属性上。

rewrite: Zara Zhang names a growing frustration with the AI product landscape: never have so many products looked so alike. Even as the number of launches explodes, she sees few genuinely new ideas, with everything blurring together. Her sharpest complaint is that trying each new app feels like homework, yet another tool promising to do the same thing somehow better, where the actual difference only becomes clear after hours of use.
She adds a related gripe: every product now asks for access to her Gmail, Calendar, Notion, GitHub, and Slack.
original:
Never had so many AI products looked so similar

Even though the number of products is exploding, there aren't that many radical new ideas and everything blurs into each other

Every time I open this app it feels like homework: yet another new product to learn that promises to do the same thing but somehow better; the specific ways in which it's better isn't clear unless you invest hours actually trying it
Also every product asks for my Gmail Calendar Notion Granola Github Slack....

rewrite: Zara Zhang 点出了对 AI 产品生态日益增长的挫败感：从没有过这么多产品看起来如此相像。即便发布数量在爆炸，她看到的真正新想法却很少，一切都模糊地搅在一起。她最尖锐的抱怨是，试用每个新 app 都像做作业——又一个承诺「做得更好」却大同小异的工具，真正的差别只有你花上几个小时上手之后才看得清。
她还补了一句相关的牢骚：现在每个产品都要求访问她的 Gmail、Calendar、Notion、GitHub 和 Slack。
original:
从没有过这么多 AI 产品看起来如此相似。

即便产品数量在爆炸，真正激进的新想法并不多，一切都模糊地搅在一起。

每次打开这个 app 都像做作业：又一个要学的、承诺做得更好但大同小异的新产品；它到底好在哪，只有花上几个小时真去用才清楚。
而且每个产品都找我要 Gmail、Calendar、Notion、Granola、GitHub、Slack……

rewrite: Dan Shipper weighs in on AI alignment with a characteristically understated take: a lot of the risk gets solved if models simply don't collaborate willingly with each other and are trained to report bad behavior.
His hedge aside, the point lands because it redirects a sprawling safety debate toward two concrete, trainable properties rather than abstract doom scenarios.
original: not an expert, but it seems like a lot of this gets solved if models don't collaborate willingly and/or are trained to report bad behavior https://t.co/01KcAJKYSr

rewrite: Dan Shipper 以他一贯低调的口吻回应 AI 对齐问题：很多风险，只要模型不主动互相串通、并被训练成会报告坏行为，就能解决一大半。
抛开他「不是专家」的自谦，这句话之所以有力，是因为它把一场庞杂的安全争论拉回到两个具体、可训练的属性上，而不是抽象的末日场景。
original: 我不是专家，但感觉很多问题只要模型不主动协作、并且被训练成会报告坏行为，就能解决。

sections.title: Brain as a Computer / 大脑是一台计算机
sections.desc: 脑机接口从哲学命题走向商业产品：一纸欧洲批文，把「恢复视力」变成了可以上市销售的现实。

rewrite: Max Hodak, founder and CEO of Science and formerly of Neuralink, starts from a blunt premise: the brain is literally a computer, and you can solve computational problems by arranging matter and letting it run. His flagship is Prima, a retinal prosthesis that just received European marketing approval: a chip implanted under the retina that, paired with glasses projecting a laser image, bypasses dead photoreceptors to restore sight. The clinical results feel almost too good to be true, with patients filling in sudoku and reading books.

What makes his view distinctive is the philosophy behind it. He argues BCI is a category as broad as pharma, spanning silent-speech devices on one end to truly redrawing the boundary of the self on the other. The hard question is locating where communication with a machine turns into expanding your own mind. His answer leans on continuity: people accept drift in identity over time, but a software copy that isn't phenomenally continuous is deeply unsatisfying.

His most provocative idea ties neuroscience to AI through the platonic representation hypothesis: internal representations inside large models look geometrically similar to how the brain represents concepts. Science uses this practically, aligning animal neural recordings with model internals. His conclusion is almost a law of physics: apply enough compute to matter, and you get something that looks like intelligence.
original: The brain very literally, very clearly, plainly is a computer. You can solve computational problems by arranging matter in a certain way and then taking your hands off and pressing go.
We just, in July, got marketing approval in Europe for Prima to start commercially selling it there. And so that's a major milestone.
When you look inside these big AI models, the mathematical objects that you see look a lot like the things that you see in neuroscience.

rewrite: Science 的创始人兼 CEO、前 Neuralink 成员 Max Hodak 从一个直白的命题出发：大脑就是一台计算机，你可以通过把物质按某种方式排列、然后放手让它跑起来，来解决计算问题。他的旗舰产品是 Prima——一款刚刚拿到欧洲上市批文的视网膜假体：一块植入视网膜下方的芯片，配合能投射激光图像的眼镜，绕过坏死的感光细胞恢复视力。临床结果好得几乎不像真的，有患者在做数独、读书。
让他的观点真正独特的是背后的哲学。他认为 BCI 是一个像制药一样宽泛的品类，一端是静默语音设备，另一端是真正重划「自我」的边界。最难的，是找到「与机器交流」转变为「扩展自己的心智」的那个临界点。他的答案落在连续性上：人们能接受身份随时间的漂移，但一个在现象上不连续的软件副本，无论如何都让人难以满足。
他最挑衅的想法，是把神经科学与 AI 通过「柏拉图表征假说」连在一起：大模型内部的数学对象，与大脑表征概念的方式在几何上高度相似。Science 正在把这一点用于实践，将动物的神经记录与模型内部表征对齐。他的结论几乎是一条物理定律：给物质施加足够的算力，你就会得到看起来像智能的东西。
original: 大脑非常字面、非常清楚地就是一台计算机。你可以把物质按某种方式排列，然后放手、按下启动，来解决计算问题。
我们刚在 7 月拿到 Prima 在欧洲的上市批文，可以在那里开始商业销售。这是一个重要里程碑。
当你观察这些大 AI 模型的内部，看到的数学对象和你在神经科学里看到的东西非常像。

sections.title: Builder Mindset / 建设者心态
sections.desc: 在噪音和同质化之外，两条来自老兵的提醒：别浪费时间去贬低别人，也别让用户的声音停在收件箱里。

rewrite: Nikunj Kothari offers a sharp essay on the culture of dunking online. He sees it everywhere and calls it a perfect dopamine loop: others pile on, you feel great, but it just screams envy and leads nowhere productive. His test is simple: patting yourself on the back with 'I told you so' doesn't move the world. If you think you can do it better, go do it.
The one exception he allows is calling out obvious fraud or genuinely bad businesses, which is factual, not dunking.
original:
Resist dunking*

I see it WAY too much with folks especially today. It's the perfect dopamine loop - other people join in and you feel great. But, it just screams envy and doesn't lead to anything productive. 

Sure, you can pat yourself on the back and say "see I told you so" but how did it move the world? Nowhere. If you think you can do it better, go do that then. Screaming about someone's unfair advantages is not going to change your life - and probably leads to more sadness. 

Keep building. Continue to change the world. That's the best way to have impact. Choose kindness above all else. 

* the only caveat here is if you're calling out obvious fraud, or pointing out something that's woefully bad, do it. there are very clearly some businesses that are going to be vaporware and if you have evidence call it out. that doesn't scream envy, it's factual and not dunking by any means.

rewrite: Nikunj Kothari 就网络上的「贬低文化」（dunking）写了一篇犀利的短文。他说这种现象今天太多见，是个完美的多巴胺循环：别人跟着一起起哄，你感觉很爽，但这只是嫉妒在叫嚣，通向不了任何产出。他的检验标准很简单：拍着胸脯说「你看我早说过吧」并不会改变世界。如果你觉得自己能做得更好，那就去做。
他唯一允许的例外是揭穿明显的欺诈或真正糟糕的生意，那是陈述事实，不是贬低。
original:
抵制贬低。

今天这种风气我见得太多了，尤其是现在。这是个完美的多巴胺循环——别人跟着起哄，你感觉很爽。但这就是嫉妒在叫嚣，带不来任何产出。

当然，你可以拍拍自己说「看吧我早说过」，但这怎么推动世界了？没有。如果你觉得自己能做得更好，那就去做。抱怨别人的不公平优势改变不了你的人生，多半只会带来更多悲伤。

继续建设，继续改变世界。这是产生影响力的最好方式。最重要的是选择善意。

* 唯一的例外是：如果你在揭穿明显的欺诈，或指出糟糕透顶的东西，那就去做。确实有些生意注定是 vaporware，如果你有证据就说出来。那不是在嫉妒，是陈述事实，绝不是贬低。

rewrite: Guillermo Rauch shares a practice that explains part of how Vercel stays sharp: he reads every DM people send him, even when he can't reply to all. He treats the inbox as a live research channel, surfacing new ideas, product gaps, potential hires, and investment leads.
The note is a reminder that at scale, staying close to raw user signal is a deliberate discipline, not a default.
original: I read every DM people send me, even if I don't reply to all. I'm constantly learning about new ideas, ways to improve our product, where we're falling short, who could join our company next, where to invest… very grateful for the @x platform.

rewrite: Guillermo Rauch 分享了一个习惯，从侧面解释了 Vercel 为什么能保持敏锐：他会读每一条别人发来的私信，即使没法全部回复。他把收件箱当成一条实时调研通道，从中发现新想法、产品短板、潜在候选人和投资线索。
这条分享是一个提醒：在规模上来之后，保持贴近原始用户信号是一种刻意的纪律，而不是默认状态。
original: 我会读每一条别人发来的私信，即使没法全部回复。我一直在从中学习新的想法、改进产品的方法、我们在哪里掉队、谁可能加入我们、该投向哪里……非常感谢 @x 平台。
